english: How do I know a good pot? Strike it for me with a stick(?), guest. A whole pot rings. A split one is silent. This one rings. That is the best to me. It is worth a goat. Now I strike another. Strike it softly. Do not break it.

I bring you the hide of a boar. My feet are cold. First I scrape off its flesh with a sharp bone. Now I smear it with fat and stretch it. How many days will you work? Nine days. The sun dries a hide slowly. What wage do you want? Leave me the boar's meat. So be it.

Craftsman, the wheel of my wagon is split. Is the axle also broken? The axle is whole. Now bring the wagon home for me. I will cut a new wheel first. Will it be strong? It will be stronger than the old one. Make it soon; it will go long (after?). Now I will work through the night.

Craftsman, my old yoke is broken. My oxen stand in the field. Who made it? My father made it. It was soft. I will carve a new one from beech. Now I rub it with a stone and bore it with an awl. How much will you take for it? Wait three nights and then come. I will lead a lamb to you.

Why do you come to me, man, for fire? The shaft of my spear is broken. Make me a new bronze point. Where is the old point? It perished and stayed in a boar. Now I want bronze, and bronze is worth much. What will you give? A boar's tusks and its hide. I take those.

My brother gave you a knife for a day. Where is your own knife? My son left it in the river. Take it. You owe much. If you break it, you will make me a new one. I will not break it. I will cut the fish. Bring it back in the evening.
